h1: The 6 Best Tablets for Reading of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Tablets for Reading 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six reading tablets and e-readers compared by screen size, storage, and price bucket, from Kindle to iPad and Fire HD.
summary: The Kindle Paperwhite 16GB is our top pick for pure reading. The Fire HD 8 is the budget all-rounder with 64GB, the Fire HD 10 adds a bigger 10.1 inch screen and stylus support, and the iPad 11-inch is for readers who want one device for everything.
intro: Reading on a screen is not one task, it is two: sitting with a novel for an hour, and flipping through magazines, PDFs, and comics. The same device rarely wins both, and buyers who pick a tablet for novels often regret the glare, while buyers who pick an e-reader for PDFs regret the small screen.
We ranked six devices from their listings: screen size, storage, and price bucket. Where a listing is thin, we say so and avoid claims it does not make.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 16GB (newest model)
products.verdict: A 7 inch e-reader with 16GB for book-first readers.
products.description:
The Kindle Paperwhite comes with a 7 inch display and 16GB of storage, and Amazon describes it as 20% faster than the prior model.

It ranks first because it focuses on reading, the task most buyers want, and sits in the $100-200 bucket. The tradeoff is that it is not a general tablet, so apps and video are out.

It suits book lovers. Check formats if you read non-Kindle files.

products.name: Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet
products.verdict: A 64GB tablet that reads and does a bit more.
products.description:
The Fire HD 8 has 64GB of storage and sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks second because it offers general tablet use for the same price bucket as the Kindles, though the listing gives few display details. The tradeoff is a backlit screen rather than e-ink.

It suits casual readers who also watch video.

products.name: Amazon Fire HD 10 tablet
products.verdict: A 10.1 inch screen with stylus support for magazines and PDFs.
products.description:
The Fire HD 10 has a 10.1 inch display, 32GB of storage, and stylus support.

It ranks third because 32GB is less than the Fire HD 8, but the bigger screen suits magazines and PDFs. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It suits readers of documents and graphic content.

products.name: Amazon Kindle 16 GB (newest model)
products.verdict: The lightest, most compact Kindle with 16GB.
products.description:
Amazon describes this Kindle as its lightest and most compact, with 16GB of storage.

It ranks fourth because it is a step below the Paperwhite in the lineup, but it sits in the same $100-200 bucket and pocketable size suits commuters.

It suits readers who value portability.

products.name: Barnes & Noble NOOK GlowLight 4 Plus eReader 7.8-inch 32GB
products.verdict: A 7.8 inch e-reader outside the Kindle ecosystem.
products.description:
The NOOK GlowLight 4 Plus has a 7.8 inch screen and 32GB of storage, in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks fifth because the ecosystem is smaller than Amazon's, but it is the cheapest e-reader here and the screen is larger than the Paperwhite's 7 inches.

It suits buyers who prefer Barnes & Noble.

products.name: Apple iPad 11-inch: A16 chip
products.verdict: An 11 inch tablet that reads and does everything else.
products.description:
The iPad has an 11 inch display, 128GB of storage, an A16 chip, and keyboard compatibility.

It ranks last for reading alone because it sits in the $200-500 bucket and is overkill for novels, but it handles PDFs, apps, and work.

It suits readers who want one device for everything.
products.idealFor: Readers who want a do-everything device.

finalTake: The Kindle Paperwhite 16GB is the best choice for readers who mostly read books. Choose the Fire HD 10 for PDFs, the Fire HD 8 for budget versatility, or the iPad for one device that does everything.
